text_837941310.text: Reimagine the direct anterior approach

text_1180487182.text: Approach direct anterior with less stress and less sweat.

text_1098967316.text: Mako Total Hip and Direct Anterior Reconstructive Technology (DART™) can help you on your journey to reduce, if not eliminate, fluoroscopy.

text.text:
Less stress 

With 3D CT-based planning and AccuStopTM haptic technology, Mako Total Hip and DART help deliver a predictable surgical experience,5-7 allowing for confidence and reducing stress.8

text_copy.text:
Less sweat

Reduce, if not eliminate, your use of fluoro and help drive efficiencies in your workflow so that you can sweat less.8-10

text_484319818.text: Potential concerns associated with fluoroscopy

text_578006142.text:
With the use of fluoroscopy in direct anterior procedures, it’s important to be aware of the potential risks fluoroscopy may pose for surgeons and OR staff.11

Click below to explore the common concerns:

text_1863295405_copy.text:
Intraoperative radiation may generate unwanted side effects such as cancer.11

 

Surgeons and OR staff may be exposed to ionizing radiation during direct anterior hip proedures.12,13 Exposure to radiation can increase the risk of unwanted side effects, including breast cancer, thyroid cancer and cataracts.12-17

text_copy_copy_copy.text: Female orthopaedic surgeons have breast cancer rates nearly 4x higher than the general population.14

text_copy_copy_20848.text: The eye's lens ranks among the body's most sensitive tissues to radiation, raising concerns about the potential for cataract development among individuals who frequently utilize fluoroscopy and do not use leaded glasses for protection.17

Studies have demonstrated that regardless of positioning or protective measures, the breast's upper outer quadrant received increased radiation exposure due to constraints in the protective lead gear design. Elevated levels of breast cancer have been reported in surgeons.14,17

text_copy_1930060299_88233043.text:
Protective lead gear (PLG) may be associated with unintended consequences for surgeons and OR staff.18-20

 

Traditionally, surgeons and their OR staff use protective lead gear (PLG) to minimize radiation exposure. However, PLGs can become less effective over time, and have been associated with several unintended side effects, such as inadequate coverage for females, physical fatigue such as back pain and bacterial contamination in the OR.14,17-20

text.text: A study of 1011 PLGs found that up to 50% showed tears and cracks within 4 years of purchase.18

text_copy_1930060299.text:
Two-dimensional images produced by fluoroscopy may not lead to better positioning of the components.21,22

 

Surgeon estimation of position on two-dimensional images have been shown to be unreliable and may be misleading.21,22 Additionally, the position of the imaging equipment has been shown to impact the accuracy of the images produced.23

text.text: A study has shown that surgeon estimations of inclination and anteversion on two-dimensional fluoroscopic images have poor reliability, with an average error of 6° in inclination and 9° in anteversion, respectively.21

text_copy.text: It has been shown that the projected image of the acetabular component can change dramatically depending on the fluoroscopic beam position relative to the hip and pelvis.24,25

Join the journey to fluoro free 

With Mako Total Hip and DART

text.text:
3D CT-based planning

Mako Total Hip’s 3D CT-based planning allows you to know more about your patient’s anatomy, helping you to stress less in the OR.5-8

Workflow efficiencies

Mako Total Hip enables single stage reaming and guided cup placement to streamline acetabular preparation without the need of intraoperative fluoroscopy helping you to sweat less.8-10

text_1799443200_copy.text: In a study, Mako Total Hip was associated with improved efficiency in workflow over manual DA with intraoperative fluoroscopy.9

text_copy_copy.text:
Direct Anterior Reconstructive Technology

DART™ is Stryker’s all-in-one solution for DA procedures, providing a comprehensive range of DA-specific products designed to enhance surgeons' experience in the OR and give you what you need, when you need it, including:​

text.text:
• Implants
 
  • Instrumentation
 
  • Patient positioning equipment 
 
  • Mako Total Hip
 
  • Education
 
  • Site of service

section_title_106497462.title: Mako Total Hip Features to Reduce or Eliminate Fluoro

text_1790685607.text:
Reduce, if not eliminate, fluoro

Reduction of fluoro seen in the direct anterior workflow

text_1040286802.text: When it comes to the direct anterior approach, where the field of view may be obscured and the use of fluoroscopy may be misleading, knowing more about a patient’s unique anatomy, having guidance while preparing the acetabulum and having a wide range of DA options can make a difference.21,22

accordion.title: Click below to see how to reduce, if not eliminate, fluoro in your DA workflow with Mako Total Hip features.

text.text: The digital ruler feature allows surgeons to plan their neck cut and measure intraoperatively, to have a more reproducible neck cut and stem placement.9

text_copy.text: Guided reaming allows surgeons to single stage ream while accurately restoring the center of rotation and achieving accurate bone preparation to plan with direct anterior.5
Guided cup placement allows surgeons to implant the cup at the desired inclination and version with direct anterior.5,26
Ability to size stem with in ±1 size due to CT-based planning and digital ruler.27
Intraoperative feedback on hip length and offset can lead to less trialing and has been shown to restore hip length and offset.28

text_2013436561.text:
"Utilizing Mako Total Hip and Stryker’s DART portfolio has allowed me to perform my total hip replacements more accurately to my plan without the need for intraoperative fluoroscopy. This has led to less stress on my body and has allowed me to be more efficient with my direct anterior hips due to not having to rely on intraoperative fluoroscopy."5,8,9,10

- Dr. Charles Claps, D.O.

Dr. Claps is a paid-consultant of Stryker Orthopaedics. The opinions expressed by Dr. Claps are those of Dr. Claps and not necessarily those of Stryker. Individual experiences may vary.
